'''Lisa J. Fauci''' (born September 21, 1960) is an American [[mathematician]] who applies [[computational fluid dynamics]] to biological processes such as [[sperm motility]] and [[phytoplankton]] dynamics.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.iciam2015.cn/Lisa%20Fauci%20HP.html|title=Speaker biography: Lisa Fauci|work=8th International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics, Beijing, China|date=August 2015|accessdate=2015-09-09|archive-date=2015-09-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918225215/http://www.iciam2015.cn/Lisa%20Fauci%20HP.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref> More generally, her research interests include [[numerical analysis]], [[scientific computing]], and [[mathematical biology]]. She is the Pendergraft Nola Lee Haynes Professor of Mathematics at [[Tulane University]],<ref>{{citation|url=http://tulane.edu/sse/math/faculty/|title=Faculty by Research Interests|publisher=Tulane University Mathematics Department|accessdate=2015-09-09|archive-date=2017-03-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170310043813/http://www2.tulane.edu/sse/math/faculty/|url-status=dead}}.</ref> and was president of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (2019–2020).<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Leadership|url=https://www.siam.org/About-SIAM/Leadership|accessdate=2019-12-11|website=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]}}</ref> She was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2023.<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=News from the National Academy of Sciences |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502194908/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 2, 2023 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=2023-05-11}}</ref>

==Education==
Fauci was born in [[Brooklyn, New York]].<ref name="bio">{{citation|url=http://dauns.math.tulane.edu/~ljf/bio.html|title=Lisa Fauci bio|accessdate=2015-09-09}}.</ref> She did her [[undergraduate]] studies at [[Pace University]], where she was encouraged to continue in mathematics by her mentor there, Michael Bernkopf.<ref name="anziam">{{citation|url=http://anziam2014.auckland.ac.nz/women-in-mathematics-lunch/|title=Q&A with the ANZIAM 2014 Female Plenary Speakers|work=ANZIAM 2014, Rotorua, New Zealand|publisher=Australian and New Zealand Industrial and Applied Mathematics|accessdate=2015-09-09}}.</ref> After earning a B.S. in mathematics in 1981,<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://math.tulane.edu/~ljf/bio8.ps|title=Curriculum vitae: Lisa J. Fauci|accessdate=2015-09-09}}.</ref> she went on to graduate studies at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of [[New York University]], completing a master's degree in 1984 and her doctorate in 1986, under the supervision of [[Charles S. Peskin]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=33111}}.</ref>

== Career ==
Fauci has been at [[Tulane University]] since 1986.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="cv" />

==Recognition==
In 2012 Fauci became a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] "for contributions to computational biofluid dynamics and applications."<ref>{{citation|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2012|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2012|accessdate=2015-09-09}}.</ref> From 2014 to 2016, Fauci served as a Council Member at Large for the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en |archive-date=2023-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306081906/https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2016 she was selected as the annual Sonia Kovalevsky Lecturer by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B2rXxbFqvn3Za1BEUmtfVlUwSlVJWFJreXFvSHVRQnpENXBR/view|title=Lisa Fauci to be AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecturer|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|date=March 28, 2015|accessdate=2016-05-01}}.</ref> In 2018, she became a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellowship|url=http://www.aps.org/units/dfd/fellowship/index.cfm|access-date=2020-06-07|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> 

In 2019 Fauci was elected fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science<ref>{{Cite web|title=AAAS Announces Leading Scientists Elected as 2019 Fellows|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science.|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-announces-leading-scientists-elected-2019-fellows|access-date=2023-04-13}}</ref> (AAAS). She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 Class, for "contributions to computational fluid dynamics and applications, and for service to the applied mathematical community".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2020 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2019-11-03}}</ref>

Fauci was elected to the 2023 class of fellows of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] "for her vision of advancing women in the mathematical sciences; for executing that vision by encouraging women to pursue graduate studies and providing sustained mentorship throughout their careers; and for opening pathways for the broader inclusion of women through her leadership in international organizations such as SIAM."<ref name="AWMfellow">{{cite web |title=The AWM Fellows Program: 2023 Class of AWM Fellows |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2023-awm-fellows/ |publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics |access-date=2022-10-23}}</ref>  She was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2023.<ref name="NAS"/> In November 2023, Fauci was a Tulane 2023 Hall of Fame winner. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Lisa Fauci: Hall of Fame Award Winner {{!}} Tulanian |url=https://tulanian.tulane.edu/winter-2024/dr-lisa-fauci-hall-fame-award-winner |access-date=2024-04-04 |website=tulanian.tulane.edu |language=en}}</ref> She is a speaker of the IBS Biomedical Mathematics Group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lisa Fauci |url=https://www.ibs.re.kr/bimag/speaker/lisa-fauci/ |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=Biomedical Mathematics Group |language=en-US}}</ref>
